title: Some simple iterated maps generate randomness intrinsically from simple seeds

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Some simple iterated maps generate randomness intrinsically from simple seeds

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Some simple iterated maps, such as taking the fractional part of 3x/2, produce behavior that looks random even when started from very simple initial numbers like 1/2, so they intrinsically generate randomness rather than transcribing it from initial conditions.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: a crucial discovery in this book is that systems like (a) and (b) on pages 150 and 151 can show behavior that seems in many respects random even when their initial conditions show no sign of randomness and are in fact extremely simple.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 4, “Systems Based on Numbers”; section “Iterated Maps and the Chaos Phenomenon” (from p. 149), p. 154. Scope: simple one-dimensional iterated maps on [0, 1]

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch04-20: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.79

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Exact arithmetic and standard tests can decisively examine the named maps and seeds over long finite ranges. They cannot prove unrestricted randomness or fully separate generated complexity from information implicit in mathematical constants and encoding.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Iterate each exactly specified map from low-description-length rational seeds and test trajectories for periodicity, compressibility, and statistical irregularity. Irregular output from a fixed simple seed supports finite-scale intrinsic generation; proof of a simple orbit would refute it for that example.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Finite-precision arithmetic can create spurious cycles.

Simplicity and intrinsic generation depend on representation.

Random-looking output is test-relative.

fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.7
data existence: 0.95
analysis feasibility: 0.94

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The maps and the simple seed are fully specified, and the contrast with the shift map is that the same seed produces irregular output. That orbit is an exact computation, reproducible at lengths far beyond the figures. A detected period would refute the example, and a persistent irregular orbit confirms the existence claim Wolfram states.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Iterate the fractional part of 3x/2, and the other simple maps Wolfram contrasts with the shift, starting from 1/2, and test digits and sizes for periodicity and statistical irregularity. Eventual periodicity or a short formula refutes intrinsic randomness from that seed; a long irregular orbit from a simple seed confirms it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Statistical irregularity of a finite orbit does not prove that the map is a randomness source in a stronger algorithmic sense.

These orbits are related to the base-2 digits of powers of 3, so a hidden structure there would also be a structure here.

operationalizability: 0.75
data existence: 0.9
data adequacy: 0.85
